WIDA stands for world-class instructional design and assessment it's a national consortium that now includes 42 states including Virginia the consortium supports states and serving serving identified English learners by providing research-based English language development standards, high quality assessments, and professional learning. In Virginia, we use two primary WIDA assessments. listening, speaking, reading, and writing. And Access is only administered once a year and right now we are currently in the testing window of this school year. Because WIDA is the foundation of how Virginia identifies and monitors English learners access plays a central role in our accountability system and any redesign would have major implications statewide the Virginia Department of Education

measures progress in English language proficiency as part of the school performance and support framework 10% of the school's overall ratings comes from how well English learners grow on the WIDA access assessment growth is determined by comparing a student's overall composite score over two consecutive years the table outlines how much growth is required based on a a student's starting proficiency level and their grade band.

So, for example, students in grades K through 2 at the lowest proficiency levels are expected to grow by one full point, while students in higher grades or higher proficiency levels have smaller growth targets. This ensures expectations are developmentally appropriate and align to realistic progress in academic English.
